<!-- EDIT: name the job this replaces (an `nb.<variable>.Boostmtree` job), and
     say which response, visit time and predictors it used.
     Replace this comment with that text. -->

An `nb-boostmtree` job fits boosted multivariate trees to a response measured
repeatedly over follow-up, one row per visit, and reports how well it fits and
what drives it: the cross-validated error path, observed against fitted values
over time, variable importance, partial effects over time, and a sample of
patients' fitted trajectories.

<!-- The two values below are written by add_job() from the subject/type it
     was called with, which are also the filename's first two fields. They
     name the SET this job belongs to, and every artifact path in the
     document is computed from them, so no output path below needs editing.

     Do NOT hand-edit these declarations: the render-time guard below checks
     them against this file's own name and stops if they disagree. To put
     this job in a different set, call add_job() again with the new
     subject/type rather than editing this copy in place.

     A set is keyed on (subject, analysis type), not on the subject alone.
     One subject may be analyzed by several methods -- parametric hazard, random
     forest survival, competing risks -- and those chains share their upstream.
     Two sets keyed on `dead_pa` alone would write their life tables to the
     same file. -->

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| results: asis
SUBJECT <- "lvef"
TYPE    <- "boost"
.in <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
# boostmtree must be the CCF fork, 2.0.8 or later. Every study fits with
# cv.flag = TRUE, and in boostmtree 2.0.0 (the CRAN release) that flag leaves the
# in-sample fit frozen, so the stored coefficients diverge with M and every
# non-cross-validated result is wrong: partial and marginal effects, importance,
# and predict(use.cv.flag = FALSE). Reported upstream as kogalur/boostmtree#2;
# the fix is kogalur/boostmtree#3. The version floor separates the fork from
# CRAN today. Should upstream release a 2.0.2 without the fix, this check would
# pass it; read the installed package's NEWS if in doubt. 2.0.8 is the floor
# because it adds the progress = argument of boostmtree() and partial.plot(), which
# the fit and the partial effects below use to report how far they have got; it
# also keeps boostmtree.control(cv.cores = ), added in 2.0.4, which the fit uses.
# 2.0.8 is also the release whose workers need about a third of 2.0.4's memory,
# each uses one BLAS thread, so a server's multithreaded OpenBLAS does not
# overload the machine, and its partial effects no longer hold every boosting
# step in memory at once.
if (!requireNamespace("boostmtree", quietly = TRUE) || utils::packageVersion("boostmtree") < "2.0.8") {
  stop("This job needs boostmtree >= 2.0.8 from the CCF fork. Install it with\n",
       "  remotes::install_github(\"ehrlinger/boostmtree_src\", subdir = \"boostmtree\", ref = \"v2.0.8-ccf\")\n",
       "then re-render.", call. = FALSE)
}
if (!requireNamespace("ggBoostedTrees", quietly = TRUE) || utils::packageVersion("ggBoostedTrees") < "0.9.0") {
  stop("This job needs ggBoostedTrees >= 0.9.0. Install it with\n",
       "  remotes::install_github(\"ehrlinger/ggBoostedTrees\")\nthen re-render.", call. = FALSE)
}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(boostmtree)
  library(ggBoostedTrees)
  library(hvtiRutilities)
})
# Without the guard in .job_setup(), an unedited job renders green over a
# meaningless analysis. Here that is a boosted fit on the template's placeholder
# response, predictors and iteration count, whose error path and effect plots
# look exactly like a result.
# To render a job you have not finished, leave a chunk out with the chunk
# option skip, giving the reason in quotes, or call hvtiRtemplates::stop_here()
# in a chunk to leave out everything below it. A draft lists each one in a
# callout; a final render refuses them, as it refuses an unresolved marker.
# ?stop_here has more.
.job <- hvtiRtemplates:::.job_setup(SUBJECT, TYPE, envir = environment())
.root <- .job$root
set_path <- .job$set_path
.provenance_data <- list()
# Saves a figure as <name>.png, .pdf and .tiff in this set's graphs/ folder (or `kind`'s),
# under the SAVE_FIGURES and FIGURES study choices.
save_figure <- function(plot, name, width = 6, height = 4, kind = "graphs", linked = FALSE) {
  hvtiRtemplates:::.save_figure(plot, set_path(kind, paste0(name, ".png")), width, height,
                                SAVE_FIGURES, FIGURES, linked)
}

# The fit, its importances and its partial effects are cached and saved through set_path(), by set, so a later render
# or job finds this set's results and no other's.
# The draft banners, if any, and the box under the title, after all the code above.
.job$notice
```

## Study choices

Edit these values for this study before rendering.

```{r}
#| label: edit-study-choices
# EDIT: the registered dataset this job reads ("built" is the study dataset).
DATASET <- "built"

# EDIT: an hvtiRdatabuild analysis set, or NULL to read the whole dataset.
ANALYSIS_SET <- NULL

# EDIT: rows to keep, dplyr::filter() style, or NULL to keep every row:
#   WHERE <- quote(age >= 18)
#   WHERE <- rlang::exprs(age >= 18, hx_chf == 1)
WHERE <- NULL

# EDIT: the patient identifier. Without "ccfid" the job uses MRN, then eMRN;
# name another column, such as "randid", if the study uses one.
ID <- "ccfid"

# EDIT: the visit time, in years. The data hold one row per visit, built
# upstream, so the time is part of what makes a row unique. With JOIN below,
# the visit time may be a column of the joined dataset alone: KEY is then
# checked on the joined rows.
TIME <- "iv_echo"

# EDIT: what makes a row unique. The ID alone does not: a patient has a row per
# visit. A duplicated visit then stops the read rather than double-counting.
KEY <- c(ID, TIME)

# Optional, and needs no edit: NULL reads the cohort alone. To join one
# registered ancillary dataset (echoes, labs), name it in JOIN. The cohort
# above decides the patients, one row each; the joined records of other
# patients are dropped and counted in the data table.
#   JOIN_VARS: the cohort columns each joined row carries; NULL carries all,
#     and a column both datasets have stops, so list only those the job needs.
#   REDUCE: NULL keeps a row per joined record, keyed on that dataset's key;
#     list(rule = "first", by = "echo_date") keeps one row per patient ("last",
#     or "nearest" with to = a cohort date column). WHERE on a joined column
#     filters the records first, so "last" with WHERE echo_type == "TTE"
#     keeps each patient's last TTE. A tie stops: picking one record
#     silently would be a hidden choice; by = c("echo_date", "echo_seq")
#     breaks it. A job that counts or models
#     patients, one row each, needs REDUCE: NULL would count every record.
#   JOIN_KEY: overrides the joined dataset's registered key.
JOIN <- NULL
JOIN_VARS <- NULL
REDUCE <- NULL
JOIN_KEY <- NULL

# EDIT: the response measured at each visit, and its kind: "continuous",
# "binary", "ordinal" or "nominal".
RESPONSE <- "<response>"
FAMILY   <- "continuous"

# EDIT: the predictors, or NULL for every other column, which is what the
# studies this template came from all did. NULL leaves out the ID, every KEY
# column, the time, the response, and any ccfid, MRN or eMRN column; it takes
# everything else, dates included. Name the predictors when the built dataset
# carries dates or derived outcomes that should not drive the fit.
PREDICTORS <- NULL

# EDIT: boosting iterations and the learning rate. Studies used 0.01 to 0.05; a
# smaller NU needs a larger M. The error path below says whether M was enough:
# the cross-validated best M should sit well inside it, not at its right edge.
M  <- 1000
NU <- 0.05

# EDIT: predictors tried at each split of each tree, or NULL for every one of
# them, boostmtree's default. Fewer than all makes the trees less alike, as in a
# random forest, at the cost of a noisier single tree; set it to reproduce a
# study that fitted with a smaller mtry. A different MTRY is a different fit, so
# it is part of the cache key.
MTRY <- NULL

# EDIT: cores for the cross-validated fit, whose cost grows with the square of
# the number of patients; about 80% of it runs in parallel, so speed levels off
# near 4 to 5 times however many cores you give it. Each core is a forked copy of
# R holding its own working data, and memory, not speed, is what limits CORES on
# a large study. Measured on the server (2026-10-19, ordinal, about 9 visits per
# patient, M = 10): peak memory at M = 10, and hours scaled to M = 1000.
#   patients   CORES   peak memory at M = 10   hours at M = 1000   session, at least
#      1,000     4            6 GB                     7            Default (16 GB)
#      1,000     8           11 GB                     5            Small (32 GB)
#      2,000     8           30 GB                    22            Medium (64 GB)
#      4,000     4           70 GB                   110            Large (128 GB); 8 cores ran out
# Memory is an upper bound at M = 10 only. The fit keeps every step, about
# 0.35 MB per step per 1,000 visits for an ordinal response, so at M = 1000 add
# about 3 GB at 1,000 patients and 11 GB at 4,000, and possibly that much again
# per core: not yet measured, so treat the sessions above as a floor. Hours scale
# with M. CORES should never exceed the session's CPUs; Windows cannot fork.
# Not part of the cache key: the fit is identical on any number of cores.
CORES <- if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") 1L else 4L

# EDIT: seeds the fit and the sample of patients the trajectory plot draws, so
# the report reproduces. Part of the cache key.
SEED <- 2026

# EDIT: the variables to draw partial effects for, or NULL for the six most
# important. N_TRACES patients are sampled for the trajectory plot; Inf draws
# every one.
EFFECT_VARIABLES <- NULL
N_TRACES <- 100

# Set TRUE after changing a choice above. A cache whose inputs changed stops the
# render instead of returning the old fit; TRUE recomputes it.
REFIT <- FALSE

# Each figure is saved to graphs/ as a PNG (for Word), and a PDF and a TIFF (for the publisher).
# SAVE_FIGURES <- FALSE saves none; FIGURES keeps only the figures whose names
# start with one of its entries, e.g. FIGURES <- c("hp-survival"). The names are the
# file names, listed for each template in the templates README.
SAVE_FIGURES <- TRUE
FIGURES <- NULL
```

## Cohort

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data
#| tbl-cap: "The data this job read"
hvtiRutilities::verify_manifest(file.path(.root, "manifest.yaml"))
.cfg <- study_config(start = .root)
job_data <- hvtiRtemplates::read_job_data(.cfg, dataset = DATASET, analysis_set = ANALYSIS_SET,
                                          where = WHERE, id = ID, key = KEY, join = JOIN, join_vars = JOIN_VARS,
                                          reduce = REDUCE, join_key = JOIN_KEY)
d <- job_data$data
.provenance_data <- c(if (exists(".provenance_data")) .provenance_data else list(), list(job_data$provenance),
                      if (!is.null(job_data$provenance_join)) list(job_data$provenance_join))
knitr::kable(job_data$record, col.names = c("Data", ""))
.selection <- attr(job_data$record, "selection")
.id <- .selection$id
# The data's own spelling of TIME and RESPONSE, matched ignoring case as the
# ID and KEY are, so "IV_ECHO" finds iv_echo. Later chunks use these names.
.resolve <- function(x) {
  hit <- match(tolower(x), tolower(names(d)))
  ifelse(is.na(hit), x, names(d)[hit])
}
.time <- .resolve(TIME)
.response <- .resolve(RESPONSE)
# The fit groups visits by patient, so the ID, the rest of KEY and the visit
# time are its structure, not its predictors; a predictor named for any of them
# would let the model learn who a patient is or when they were seen. A known
# identifier column is never a predictor either, whatever ID names: boostmtree
# keeps its predictors, so one would reach the cache and the saved fit.
.not_predictors <- unique(c(.id, .selection$key, .time, "ccfid", hvtiRtemplates:::.job_identifier_names))
if (is.null(PREDICTORS)) {
  .identifiers <- names(d)[tolower(names(d)) %in% c("ccfid", hvtiRtemplates:::.job_identifier_names) & names(d) != .id]
  .predictors <- names(d)[!tolower(names(d)) %in% tolower(c(.not_predictors, .response))]
  if (length(.identifiers)) {
    cat("Identifier columns left out of the predictors: ", paste(.identifiers, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  }
} else {
  .predictors <- PREDICTORS
}
.duplicated <- unique(.predictors[duplicated(.predictors)])
if (length(.duplicated)) {
  stop("PREDICTORS names a variable more than once: ", paste(.duplicated, collapse = ", "), ".", call. = FALSE)
}
.structural <- .predictors[tolower(.predictors) %in% tolower(.not_predictors)]
if (length(.structural)) {
  stop("PREDICTORS names an identifier, a KEY column or the visit time: ", paste(.structural, collapse = ", "),
       ".", call. = FALSE)
}
# The response predicting itself would fit perfectly and mean nothing.
if (tolower(.response) %in% tolower(.predictors)) {
  stop("PREDICTORS names the response (", .response, ").", call. = FALSE)
}
# Nor may an identifier be the response or the visit time: boostmtree keeps
# both, so one would reach the cache and the saved fit. That covers the ID this
# job uses and any other identifier column the data carry, such as a ccfid
# beside an ID of randid.
.identifier_cols <- c(.id, "ccfid", hvtiRtemplates:::.job_identifier_names)
if (tolower(.response) %in% tolower(.identifier_cols)) {
  stop("A patient identifier (", .response, ") cannot be the response.", call. = FALSE)
}
if (tolower(.time) %in% tolower(.identifier_cols)) {
  stop("A patient identifier (", .time, ") cannot be the visit time.", call. = FALSE)
}
.missing <- setdiff(c(.time, .response, .predictors), names(d))
if (length(.missing)) {
  stop("Not in the data this job read: ", paste(.missing, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
}
d <- d[, c(.id, .time, .response, .predictors), drop = FALSE]
# boostmtree imputes a missing predictor but cannot learn from a visit with no
# response, so those visits are dropped here, and counted.
.no_response <- is.na(d[[.response]])
if (any(.no_response)) {
  cat(sum(.no_response), " visit(s) have no ", .response, " and are left out.\n", sep = "")
  d <- d[!.no_response, , drop = FALSE]
}
.chr <- .predictors[vapply(d[.predictors], is.character, logical(1L))]
if (length(.chr)) {
  d[.chr] <- lapply(d[.chr], factor)
  cat("Text predictors converted to factors: ", paste(.chr, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: data-attrition
#| results: asis
# unnumbered: its child chunk carries its own label and caption
if (!is.null(job_data$attrition)) {
  .fence <- strrep("`", 3)
  cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(
    paste0(.fence, "{r}"), "#| label: tbl-data-attrition",
    paste0("#| tbl-cap: ", encodeString(paste0("Analysis set `", ANALYSIS_SET, "`: exclusions, in order"), quote = "\"")),
    "knitr::kable(job_data$attrition)", .fence
```

## Fit

```{r}
#| label: fit
#| message: true
# The fit groups visits by patient through `id`. It is given the study-keyed
# digest of each patient's ID, not the ID: a boostmtree fit stores the ID in
# several places, its base learners included, and every one of them is saved
# with it. A digest still groups the visits; it cannot be read back.
CACHE_DIR <- dirname(set_path("estimates", "nb-boostmtree.rds"))
# The fit runs for hours at study size. Started from the console it dies with
# the session, so an uncached fit is refused there: run the job with
# hvtiRtemplates::submit_job() instead. Once cached, these chunks load it.
hvtiRtemplates::guard_long_fit("nb-boostmtree-fit", dir = CACHE_DIR,
                               why = "a cross-validated boostmtree fit takes hours at study size",
                               refit = REFIT)
.patient <- hvtiRtemplates:::.id_digest(d[[.id]], hvtiRtemplates:::.study_id_key(.root))
fit <- cache_fit(
  "nb-boostmtree-fit",
  boostmtree(x = d[.predictors], tm = d[[.time]], id = .patient, y = d[[.response]],
             family = FAMILY, M = M, nu = NU, mtry = MTRY, mod.grad = TRUE, cv.flag = TRUE, verbose = FALSE,
             # get() keeps CORES out of cache_fit()'s key, which sees only the values
             # the call names directly: changing it must not mark an identical fit stale.
             control = boostmtree.control(cv.cores = get("CORES")),
             # Reports each boosting iteration to <job>.run.progress and the render log.
             # get() keeps the job's run record out of the cache key's inputs, as for
             # CORES: it changes what is reported, never what is fitted.
             progress = get(".job")$progress("iteration")),
  seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT
)
```

`cv.flag = TRUE` and `mod.grad = TRUE` are not settings. Every study fitted with
both, and cross-validation is how the job chooses its best number of iterations.

## Does the fit work?

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fit
#| tbl-cap: "The fit"
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  quantity = c("Family", "Iterations (M)", "Learning rate (nu)", "Patients", "Visits"),
  value = c(FAMILY, M, NU, length(unique(.patient)), nrow(d))
), col.names = c("", ""))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fit-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Cross-validated fit, by response component"
# A continuous or binary fit has one response component; an ordinal or nominal
# fit has one per level after the first, each with its own cross-validated best
# M and error path (fit$err.rate is then a list). Read the error at the best M
# from the standardized l2 column, the scale gg_boost_error() plots.
.err <- if (is.matrix(fit$err.rate)) list(fit$err.rate) else fit$err.rate
# Each component is named by the level that defines it, which boostmtree keeps
# in fit$q.set: a threshold for an ordinal fit, a class compared against the
# reference class for a binary or nominal one. partial.plot() selects a
# component by the same label ("response" for a continuous fit).
.labels <- if (identical(fit$family, "continuous")) "response" else as.character(fit$q.set)
.reference <- setdiff(as.character(fit$y.levels), .labels)
# An ordinal component is a cumulative logit at its threshold, but boostmtree's
# documentation does not say which side of the threshold it models, so the
# label names the threshold only. (Its 2.0.2 source codes P(y <= k); read the
# installed package before relying on that.)
.components <- switch(fit$family,
  continuous = .response,
  binary = ,
  nominal = paste(.response, "=", .labels, "against", paste(.reference, collapse = ", ")),
  ordinal = paste(.response, "threshold", .labels)
)
fit_summary <- data.frame(
  component = .components,
  best_m = as.integer(fit$m.opt),
  cv_error = mapply(function(e, m) e[m, "l2"], .err, fit$m.opt)
)
knitr::kable(fit_summary, col.names = c("Response component", "Best M (cross-validated)",
                                        "Cross-validated error there (standardized)"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-error
#| fig-cap: "Cross-validated error by boosting iteration. The black solid line is the error after each iteration, and the
#|   black dashed vertical line marks the iteration with the lowest error, Best M."
# The cross-validated error by iteration, and the fitted rho, phi and lambda.
# Best M at the right edge means M was too small.
p_error <- plot(gg_boost_error(fit)) + hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12)
save_figure(p_error, "nb-boostmtree-error")
p_error
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-path
#| fig-cap: "Fitted rho, phi and lambda by boosting iteration, one panel per parameter. Each black solid line is the
#|   parameter's fitted value after each iteration."
#| fig-height: 8
# Free size: three stacked panels, one per parameter.
p_path <- plot(gg_boost_path(fit)) + hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12)
save_figure(p_path, "nb-boostmtree-path", height = 8)
p_path
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-calibration
#| fig-cap: "Observed against fitted values over follow-up, in time bins. Each gray horizontal segment spans a time bin at
#|   its observed mean, with a vertical black bar for the interval around it; black circles mark the observed means,
#|   black triangles the fitted means, and the black dashed line joins the fitted means over time."
# Observed against fitted values over follow-up, in time bins.
# The manuscript theme hides the legend and its title, and the caption reads the shapes from the legend.
p_calibration <- plot(gg_boost_calibration(fit)) +
  hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12, legend.position = "top", legend.title = ggplot2::element_text())
save_figure(p_calibration, "nb-boostmtree-calibration")
p_calibration
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-importance
#| fig-cap: "Importance of each predictor's main effect and of its interaction with time, one panel for each. Horizontal
#|   dark gray bars give the importance of each predictor."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 7
# Importance of each predictor's main effect and its interaction with time; the
# interaction is where a predictor whose effect changes over follow-up shows.
# vimp.boostmtree() permutes each predictor at random, so it is seeded and
# cached like the fit. Unseeded, the importances moved from render to render,
# and with them the six variables the effects below are drawn for.
vimp <- cache_fit("nb-boostmtree-vimp", vimp.boostmtree(fit), seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT)
# Free size: one row per predictor, and one panel per effect, at the 6.5 in page width.
p_vimp <- plot(gg_boost_vimp(vimp)) + hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12)
save_figure(p_vimp, "nb-boostmtree-importance", width = 6.5, height = 7)
p_vimp
```

```{r}
#| label: effects
#| results: asis
# unnumbered: each child chunk below carries its own label and caption
# Partial effects over time, for EFFECT_VARIABLES or the six most important.
# An ordinal or nominal fit reports importance once per response component, so
# a variable is ranked by its largest importance across them.
.vimp_main <- gg_boost_vimp(vimp, components = "main")
.top <- sort(tapply(.vimp_main$importance, as.character(.vimp_main$variable), max), decreasing = TRUE)
.effect_vars <- if (is.null(EFFECT_VARIABLES)) head(names(.top), 6L) else EFFECT_VARIABLES
.unknown <- setdiff(.effect_vars, .predictors)
if (length(.unknown)) stop("EFFECT_VARIABLES names no predictor: ", paste(.unknown, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
# One partial.plot() covers every response component: ggBoostedTrees 0.9.0 and
# later take an ordinal or nominal one whole and facet its figure by component.
# Each component is renamed as the fit summary names it, not by its bare level.
.fence <- strrep("`", 3)
.seen <- new.env()
.child <- function(label, caption, code, opts = NULL) {
  label <- gsub("(^-+|-+$)", "", gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "-", tolower(label)))
  if (!is.null(.seen[[label]])) stop("Two outputs would share the label ", label, ".", call. = FALSE)
  .seen[[label]] <- TRUE
  .opt <- paste0("#| ", sub("-.*$", "", label), "-cap: ", encodeString(caption, quote = "\""))
  cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(paste0(.fence, "{r}"), paste0("#| label: ", label), .opt, opts, code, .fence),
                        envir = parent.frame(), quiet = TRUE), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n")
}
# partial.plot() is the slowest step after the fit: one prediction over every
# patient per grid value, 25 values per continuous covariate. It is cached
# beside the fit and keyed on it, so a re-render that changes only prose skips
# it, and a refit or a changed EFFECT_VARIABLES stops until REFIT, as the fit does.
.partial <- cache_fit("nb-boostmtree-partial",
                      partial.plot(fit, x.var.names = .effect_vars, output = "data", verbose = FALSE,
                                   progress = get(".job")$progress("prediction")),
                      seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT)
.effect <- gg_boost_effect(.partial)
.relabel <- .components[match(levels(.effect$response), .labels)]
# A component ggBoostedTrees names differently from the fit would otherwise be
# drawn under a blank label; stop and say so instead.
if (anyNA(.relabel)) {
  stop("ggBoostedTrees labels a response component this job does not recognize: ",
       paste(levels(.effect$response)[is.na(.relabel)], collapse = ", "), ".", call. = FALSE)
}
levels(.effect$response) <- .relabel
# What ggBoostedTrees 0.9.0 still cannot do: a continuous covariate is drawn as
# a curve and a factor as a point per level, on axes ggplot2 cannot share, so
# plot() refuses an effect holding both. Each kind is drawn in its own figure,
# which is why p_effects is a list.
.discrete <- tapply(!is.na(.effect$x_label), .effect$variable, any)
.discrete <- .discrete[!is.na(.discrete)]
.parts <- split(names(.discrete), .discrete)
.kinds <- ifelse(names(.parts) == "TRUE", "categorical", "continuous")
# Free size, paged: one facet per predictor, two by two on a page no larger than
# 6.5 by 9 in. With several response components ggBoostedTrees draws one column
# per predictor and one row per component, so a page holds two predictors.
.n_components <- nlevels(.effect$response)
.pages <- lapply(unname(.parts), function(v) {
  if (.n_components > 1L) {
    hvtiRtemplates:::.figure_pages(length(v), panel_height = 3 * .n_components, page_height = 3 * .n_components)
  } else {
    hvtiRtemplates:::.figure_pages(length(v), page_height = 6)
  }
})
# One plot per page, kind by kind: p_effects holds every page, and .effect_page says which kind and page each is.
p_effects <- list()
.effect_page <- list()
for (.k in seq_along(.parts)) {
  for (.j in seq_along(.pages[[.k]])) {
    part <- .effect[.effect$variable %in% .parts[[.k]][.pages[[.k]][[.j]]$index], , drop = FALSE]
    part$variable <- droplevels(part$variable)
    # The manuscript theme hides the legend and its title, and the caption reads the time colors from the legend.
    p_effects[[length(p_effects) + 1L]] <- plot(part) +
      hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12, legend.position = "top", legend.title = ggplot2::element_text())
    .effect_page[[length(.effect_page) + 1L]] <- list(kind = .kinds[[.k]], page = .j, of = length(.pages[[.k]]),
                                                      size = .pages[[.k]][[.j]], vars = levels(part$variable))
  }
}
.key <- c(continuous = paste("Each solid line is the effect at one follow-up time, colored from dark to light blue by",
                             "time as in the color bar."),
          categorical = paste("Each point is the effect at one level and follow-up time, colored from dark to light blue by",
                              "time as in the color bar."))
for (.i in seq_along(p_effects)) {
  .p <- p_effects[[.i]]
  .pg <- .effect_page[[.i]]
  save_figure(.p, sprintf("nb-boostmtree-effects-%s-page-%02d", .pg$kind, .pg$page),
              width = .pg$size$width, height = .pg$size$height)
  .on_page <- if (.pg$of > 1L) paste0(" Page ", .pg$page, " of ", .pg$of, ": ", paste(.pg$vars, collapse = ", "), ".") else ""
  .child(paste("fig effects", .pg$kind, .pg$page),
         paste0("Partial effects over follow-up, ", .pg$kind, " predictors, one panel per predictor. ", .key[[.pg$kind]],
                .on_page),
         ".p", opts = c(sprintf("#| fig-width: %g", .pg$size$width), sprintf("#| fig-height: %g", .pg$size$height)))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-traces
#| fig-cap: "Fitted trajectories for a sample of patients, with the cohort's mean fitted value over time. Thin translucent
#|   black lines trace each sampled patient's fitted values, translucent black circles their observed values, and the
#|   thick black line the cohort's mean fitted value within ten time bins."
# Fitted trajectories for a sample of patients, with their observed values as
# points, and the cohort's mean fitted value over time drawn across them. The
# patients are labeled by digest, so none is identified.
traces <- gg_boost_trajectory(fit)
# Visit times are irregular, so most exact times belong to one patient, and a
# mean taken at each time would join single values. The mean is taken instead
# within ten equal-count time bins, over every patient's fitted values, and
# drawn at each bin's mean time. A bin is per response component when there
# are several.
.edges <- unique(stats::quantile(traces$time, seq(0, 1, length.out = 11L), names = FALSE))
# plot() reports that it chose the patients at random; SEED makes the choice
# the same on every render.
p_traces <- withr::with_seed(SEED, plot(traces, n_max = N_TRACES)) + ggplot2::labs(x = .time, y = .response) +
  hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12)
if (length(.edges) < 2L) {
  # Every visit at one time leaves no span to bin, and no line to draw.
  trace_means <- NULL
  cat("Every visit is at one time, so no mean line is drawn.\n")
} else {
  traces$.bin <- cut(traces$time, .edges, include.lowest = TRUE)
  .by <- intersect(c("response", ".bin"), names(traces))
  trace_means <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(traces, traces[.by], drop = TRUE), function(b) {
    data.frame(b[1L, setdiff(.by, ".bin"), drop = FALSE], time = mean(b$time), fitted = mean(b$fitted),
               n_patients = length(unique(b$id)))
  }))
  p_traces <- p_traces +
    ggplot2::geom_line(data = trace_means, ggplot2::aes(x = .data[["time"]], y = .data[["fitted"]]),
                       linewidth = 1.2, inherit.aes = FALSE)
}
save_figure(p_traces, "nb-boostmtree-traces")
p_traces
```

```{r}
#| label: save
# The product of this job. It is separate from the cache on purpose: the cache
# is this job's internals and this file its interface, which carries the
# selection a later job would rebuild the rows from.
fit <- hvtiRtemplates:::.attach_handoff_lineage(
  fit,
  data = .provenance_data,
  analysis = list(response = .response, time = .time, family = FAMILY, M = M, nu = NU),
  cohort = list(n_patients = length(unique(.patient)), n_visits = nrow(d)),
  selection = attr(job_data$record, "selection")
)
saveRDS(fit, set_path("estimates", "nb-boostmtree.rds"))
```
